items.title: ‘Nothing About This Was Inevitable’
items.description: The second floor of OpenAI’s old headquarters had a theme. Each room was named after one of the most important inventions in human history: “Clock,” “Fire,” and, of course, “AGI,” or artificial general intelligence. I saw this in the spring of 2024, when I was interviewing some of the company’s researchers about recent technical advances . At the time, ChatGPT was still making embarrassing arithmetic errors, and the notion that the bot would ever rival human intelligence was dubious. But here, in the renovated shell of a former mayonnaise factory in San Francisco, AGI’s arrival was predestined. This belief in AGI—a computer program with capabilities that rival or even exceed those of the human mind—is foundational to the mission of Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic, three of the most influential AI companies in the world. And the pursuit of that milestone is the subject of The AGI Chronicles , a new book by the tech reporter and Atlantic contributing writer Kevin Roose, which he describes as his attempt to document the decade “when the human monopoly on advanced intelligence ended, and a new world was born.” Roose, a prominent and well-connected commenter on the AI boom, follows the internecine world of the frontier AI companies in remarkable, at times almost insular, detail. Based on interviews with more than 150 researchers, executives, investors, and policy makers close to the technology’s development, The AGI Chronicles traces crucial moments across DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic from 2015 through early 2026 to figure out how we got to this very messy moment in AI , and who’s responsible for what happens next. [ Read: The singularity is not what it seems ] If you scan statements from executives such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, there is a sense of fatalism about the rise of AI. In my conversation with Amodei last year, he likened developing AI to operating an out-of-control bus: It can’t be stopped or even slowed, but perhaps it can be steered. In an interview last month, Altman called AI “an inevitability.” According to this framing, AI executives are simply conductors, doing their best to provide guardrails for an era that’s careering our way, whether anyone likes it or not. Roose’s book prompted me to consider a question that is often neglected in the mile-a-minute news cycle: Are the leading AI companies simply heralding an inevitable evolution of this technology, as many of them claim, or are they directing that advancement? The answer will have tremendous bearing on how we assign responsibility for the world taking shape around us. The AGI Chronicles is of both minds on the topic. On the one hand, Roose is very explicit that he is archiving decisions made by a small group of people. “AGI was not inevitable,” he writes, but “invented, developed, and commercialized by a few hundred people.” On the other hand, sometimes the book reads like a natural history, describing a procession of events outside the control of any specific group of people, an almost geologic force sweeping the planet as “a new world was born.” He notes how, throughout the years, various companies and officials had yet to “wake up.” By 2024, he writes, “the idea of going back to the old world, to a time before all this, seemed more delusional than expecting the exponential to continue.” At times, Roose’s book echoes the loss of agency professed by AI executives. Of course, the inevitability of any one outcome is a self-serving fabrication. There is no prophecy that a handful of Silicon Valley companies dictating their own rules, running roughshod over copyright law and environmental regulations while mucking up once-reliable internet services with AI features nobody asked for, will operate largely unencumbered. Industries take shape through decisions made by individual actors and investors, the collective desire of the public, and the action or inaction of regulators. If you look to the late 1800s, for example, it would have seemed likely that electric cars would dominate the market in the following century. America’s best-selling car in 1897 was electric, and in the 1910s, Henry Ford was trying to develop an electric car with Thomas Edison. But a series of technological limitations and human decisions—including various financial missteps and harsh criticism from advocates of petrol-powered cars—changed the course of history, leaving a legacy that we’re reckoning with more than a century later. In the 1950s, it seemed as if nuclear reactors were destined to dot the nation and power the future. But a series of political campaigns and spectacular errors—the anti-nuclear movement, Three Mile Island, Chernobyl—crushed the nuclear age before it ever really started. Then there was the Space Age and supersonic flight—there are so many seemingly inevitable technological eras that never quite made it, not so much because of technology itself as because of political and economic choices. There are, similarly, so many corporate behemoths—Standard Oil, Kodak, Bear Stearns—that, because of regulation or complacency or fraud, unraveled. The inverse holds for many technologies and companies considered inevitable today: Different regulatory environments, international agreements, or priorities for Pentagon labs could have stopped the development of an open and global internet, smartphones, social media. When I recently called Roose to discuss his book and ask what he made of the industry’s frequently prophetic tone, he initially told me he believes that “nothing about this was inevitable. These were decisions made by people.” But he then said that he wanted to “complicate” that: “Once scaling the transformer worked, and once the scaling laws were documented,” Roose said, “I think it was inevitable that the companies building this stuff would push it as far as they possibly could.” I’d like to further complicate that view. Beyond the urge to test the bounds of any technology and reap enormous profits, the industry has been shaped by very human decisions. AI researchers chose to train their models on troves of copyrighted works without seeking permission, leading to countless creators suddenly getting left out of the economic equation. OpenAI chose to rush a free-to-use ChatGPT to the market in late 2022, kicking off a hype cycle and a subsequent investment bonanza. Venture-capital, private-equity, and tech firms chose to sink untold billions into a still-unprofitable technology. Data-center developers chose to eschew solar panels in favor of combustion turbines, which they perceive as faster and more reliable. On the government side, Donald Trump has chosen to ignore or eliminate any substantive federal regulation of AI. An industry that negotiated royalty payments, prioritized clean energy, gave itself longer development cycles, or faced serious federal regulation might look entirely different. The question of inevitability and responsibility may sound arcane, but it has real ramifications. In the Bay Area, tied up with the myth of AI’s inevitability is a sort of spiritual devotion: “Thank you to the machines, and the structure of reality, for letting us understand a little more,” Altman wrote on X this week. The more you treat AI as inevitable, the more it seems like a cosmic force rather than a product resulting from industrial and commercial design choices. The more you treat AI as inevitable, the less you can hold any company or person responsible for things going wrong. The executives, in this view, are only fractionally more empowered than us in deciding what happens next; more important, everyone else needs to wake up. As Altman put it to Politico earlier this month, “The world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology.” In the months since Roose concluded his reporting, the AI industry and its products have risen to still-greater global prominence and triggered even greater fears. When I asked him what new chapters he might add if he were still writing, Roose said that he would end the book with the recent White House press conference in which Trump, Amodei, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Elon Musk, and several other tech executives addressed AI-safety concerns. He recalled a speech Amodei gave in Anthropic’s early days about how different parts of society would gradually become attuned to the transformative effects of this technology, beginning with AI firms and ending with the state. It felt, Roose told me, “like the prophecy had been fulfilled.”

items.title: Suspended fine for Xhaka over Covid-19 certificate
items.description: Sunderland and Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka says he has received a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000) for obtaining a forged Covid-19 vaccination certificate. The 34-year-old, who is alleged to have obtained the certificate in 2022, when it was required in Switzerland for travel abroad, says the fine is suspended for two years, provided he does not commit any further offences, and that he has already paid the court costs. “A few weeks ago, I spoke personally here and said that I would take responsibility for my decision. I stand by that,” the midfielder wrote in German on Instagram. “I was sentenced by summary judgment for obtaining a false certification to a suspended fine of 50 daily rates of CHF 3,000 [£2,726] each. “I accept the decision and take responsibility for my actions. Thank you for the many messages of support over the past few weeks. They mean a lot to me.” Xhaka was playing for Arsenal in 2022 and posted a statement on social media on 21 September saying he had a “mistrust” towards the vaccine and that he had been “influenced by worries and uncertainty”. He is Switzerland’s record appearance holder with 152 caps and, following his initial statement, withdrew from his country’s camp for their Nations League matches against Scotland, North Macedonia and Slovenia in the international break that has just concluded. The Swiss office of public health had confirmed that while there was never a general legal requirement to obtain or hold such a certificate, it was needed for access to various activities, venues and travel, meaning that participation was restricted for anyone who did not possess one. These measures in Switzerland were in place until the spring of 2022. After that point, Covid-19 certificates continued to be issued, primarily to enable members of the public to meet entry requirements when travelling abroad. Xhaka captained Switzerland at the World Cup earlier this year, where they were knocked out in the quarter-finals by eventual runners-up Argentina. He is expected to return to action when Sunderland host Brighton on Saturday (15:00 BST). Black Cats boss Regis le Bris said: “No comment on external topics but [from] what I’ve seen during the international break, he has trained really well. It’s positive. He’s in a good place football-wise and for me that is the most important.”

items.title: Trump’s Team of Mercenaries
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. Kimberly Guilfoyle was so close to getting it right. The Trump hanger-on—former fiancée to Don Jr. and the current ambassador to Greece—was exchanging messages with a man named Eric Deters, according to a bombshell Wall Street Journal story last night. Deters, a right-wing podcast host, failed political candidate, and suspended lawyer in Kentucky, wanted help in clearing up some tax issues, and also wanted the Trump administration to extradite a doctor whose alleged fraud victims he was advising in a legal case. Guilfoyle, the messages indicate, wanted money—in one instance, a $100,000 wire—and she wanted it untraceable. Guilfoyle was right to worry about secrecy. She was about to begin confirmation hearings for her ambassadorship, and understood the pay-to-play could hurt her. Yet neither she nor Deters could stop breaking the Stringer Bell rule by recording their skullduggery in writing. “It won’t show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express,” Guilfoyle wrote. “Please.” And in another: “Honey please I need you to get this done for me today.” Yet even as she laid these instructions out, she kept haranguing Deters for indiscretion. “I really wish you would stop papering all these things. It’s really dangerous and not helpful to you or me while you could simply just call me on signal,” she wrote, referring to the encrypted messaging app. In one message, she wrote, “If you write an email or a text about, l’m gonna kill you cause I love you but you’re so out of control.” Unfortunately for Guilfoyle, her Signal messages were not as safe a space as she might have wished. (The Journal does not reveal how it viewed the messages. Guilfoyle’s lawyer broadly disputed their authenticity to the paper but offered no details.) Somehow, this is not the only Trump scandal with Balkan ties in the news this week. The New York Times reported that James Blair and Chris LaCivita, who are ostensibly President Trump’s top political advisers, traveled—during an intense midterm campaign in which Republicans appear to be on the verge of serious setbacks—to advise a candidate in Bosnia and Herzegovina’s self-governing Serbian entity. Both of these stories show the way that many people in Trump’s orbit view their positions not as public service but as a profit center. There’s a long and often depressing pattern of former officials capitalizing on government and political work, but Trump’s aides aren’t even willing to wait until they take their leave to start taking. Forget a team of rivals. Trump world is a team of mercenaries, in some cases literally . Jared Kushner, who was a senior adviser in his first presidency and is married to his daughter Ivanka, continues to work as an envoy for Trump while pursuing business deals around the world. As Dexter Filkins wrote in The New Yorker in September, Kushner’s record as a diplomat is underwhelming, yet his financial gains have been enormous. “He represents a new kind of Washington figure, for whom public office serves as a means to extraordinary wealth,” Filkins wrote. Kushner and Ivanka Trump even have their own Balkan boondoggle, an attempt to develop an island in Albania that has run into legal and political difficulties. Earlier this year, the Times reported that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick helped negotiate access to Kazakh tungsten reserves for an American mining company, and the federal government provided $1.6 billion in financing. Lutnick’s sons and Trump’s sons are both involved with companies that stand to profit from the deal (though representatives for them have said that they did not play a role in the deal). A Washington Post investigation this summer noted that Trump’s sons have invested heavily in defense-technology companies; the companies have scored “at least $3.2 billion in direct government business since the sons invested and an additional $3.1 billion in future contract options.” (Company representatives told the Post that they secured their business without assistance from Trump’s sons.) Where do any of these people get the idea that this is appropriate or that they can get away with it? From the president himself, naturally. Trump has moved on from small-scale grifts such as charging the Secret Service exorbitant fees to stay in his hotels during his first term to far more ambitious and lucrative schemes such as crypto ventures ; even conservative estimates put his gains during this term alone in the billions. Though Trump doesn’t have ethical scruples, he does have a sense of right and wrong: It’s right for him to profiteer, but wrong for others to make too much money from his name. That’s where Blair, LaCivita, and Guilfoyle may run into trouble. Politico reports that Republicans’ “knives are now fully out” for the two consultants. Trump himself weighed in on Truth Social , saying he was unaware of their clients but adding that he “will, on reflection, ask them and, if there’s a conflict, I will terminate them, immediately!” Firing them just before the midterms seems risky, as it might just create more chaos for Republicans, but they could make for good scapegoats after the fact. Trump has not spoken publicly about the Guilfoyle story, although Vice President Vance said he didn’t “ love that .” In a further embarrassment, the article emerged while Secretary of State Marco Rubio was visiting Athens. Perhaps inevitably, Guilfoyle’s relationship with Deters ended acrimoniously. “I have paid you $300,000 over the years,” he wrote her in 2025, adding, in an amusingly self-negating flourish, “As of this memo, I have not received one favor. I am not naive or a sucker.” She was not happy, either. “What a nightmare you’ll literally cost me my ambassadorship stop writing,” she told him at one point, per the Journal . Her warning may have been too late. Related: MAGA is making the world safe for corruption. The watchdogs are barking themselves hoarse. Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : Helen Lewis on the simple truth behind Jane Doe’s story Kathy Hochul’s improbable turnaround How the polls could be wrong again Today’s News U.S. prosecutors charged Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, with conspiring to torture Americans and other prisoners in Venezuela to suppress opposition and maintain power. The new charge has been added to the federal case against the couple, who are scheduled for trial in June 2027. At least 30 people were killed in a Russian strike on a bus in eastern Ukraine, a day after another Russian strike killed 22 people in an apartment building. The attacks come as Russia intensifies its use of drones, missiles, and guided bombs against Ukrainian targets. Hurricane Isaias strengthened into the first hurricane of the Atlantic season as it approached the Gulf Coast, and landfall is expected as soon as tomorrow. It could reach Category 3 strength, prompting hurricane watches and mandatory evacuations in parts of Florida. Dispatches Time-Travel Thursdays : In 1987, two writers predicted a path to energy independence from the Middle East. What they didn’t anticipate was what the U.S. would do to get there , Rafaela Jinich writes. Video Village : David Sims lists the decade’s 10 most defining movies (so far). Work in Progress : Rogé Karma explains the biggest source of inequality that no one talks about. Explore all of our newsletters here. Evening Read Illlustration by Hannah Robinson Forgive the Bad Texters By Julie Beck Whenever I receive a text, this is what happens. I pick up my phone. So far, so good. I experience whatever emotion the message elicits—the pleasant warmth of being reached out to, possibly the annoyance of being interrupted. Then, if conditions are right, if I’m not too busy or in the middle of talking with someone else, if my mind is at peace, if my anxiety is at no more than a low hum, if Mercury is not in retrograde, I will respond right then and there. If conditions are not right, it will be as though the text never existed at all. Read the full article. More From The Atlantic Michael Powell: “What I saw at New York’s anti-Israel October 7 rallies” Radio Atlantic : Why FBI officials are worried about the midterms If you want a real digital commons, build it yourself. Reducing the number of generals isn’t the problem. OpenAI just carpet-bombed mathematics. Culture Break Graeme Mitchell / Redux Explore. Anne Carson, the winner of this year’s Nobel Prize in Literature, makes ancient texts feel tantalizingly new , Walt Hunter writes. Take a look. An ambitious retrospective examines the life and work of Jackson Pollock and Lee Krasner—to brilliant effect, Sebastian Smee writes. Play our daily crossword. Rafaela Jinich contributed to this newsletter. When you buy a book using a link in this newsletter, we receive a commission. Thank you for supporting The Atlantic .

items.title: Businessman dragged to court over GH¢480,000 fraud
items.description: A 44-year-old businessman has appeared before an Accra Circuit Court on charges of allegedly defrauding a businesswoman of GH¢480,000. Anthony Appiah, charged with defrauding by false pretences, pleaded not guilty. The court admitted him to bail in the sum of GH¢500,000 with two sureties, one of whom must be a public servant earning not less than GH¢4,000. Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Emmanuel Nyamekye led the prosecution. The prosecution said the complainant, whose name was withheld, was a businesswoman who resided in Accra, as did Appiah. It said in May 2025, Appiah, who had known the complainant for some time, visited her home and told her that he had secured a distribution contract with BEL-AQUA Company. He allegedly said he needed $50,000 to execute the contract and appealed to the complainant for financial assistance, promising to refund the money within two weeks. The complainant subsequently gave Appiah GH¢480,000. However, after the two-week period elapsed, Appiah failed to refund the money. The prosecution said the complainant contacted BEL-AQUA Company to verify the contract and was informed that Appiah had no such contract with the company. All efforts to recover the money proved unsuccessful, prompting the complainant to petition the Police to investigate. Appiah was subsequently arrested, and investigations established that BEL-AQUA Company had neither awarded him any contract nor engaged him in any capacity.

items.title: Drame conjugal : Deux jours après ses noces, Racky Diaby tuée par balle en plein sommeil
items.description: ​ Au Mali, Racky Diaby aurait été tuée par son mari à peine deux jours après son Kognosso , la période de lune de miel qui suit le mariage. Célébrée le 27 septembre 2026, leur union aurait tourné au drame quelques jours plus tard. Selon les premiers témoignages, son époux, sous l’emprise de stupéfiants, lui aurait tiré une balle alors qu'elle dormait. ​ Le témoignage de la maquilleuse enfonce le mari de Racky ​Le témoignage de la maquilleuse qui a préparé la mariée le jour de la cérémonie est très relayé. Elle affirme avoir reçu un appel de Racky Diaby peu avant le drame. La jeune femme lui aurait confié que son mari, fils d’un ancien ministre malien, était très en colère. Il lui reprochait d'avoir publié sur les réseaux sociaux une vidéo du mariage, car il ne voulait pas que des images de son épouse circulent en ligne. ​Toujours selon la professionnelle, l'époux aurait même menacé de porter plainte contre elle. Elle précise qu'il continuait de crier sur Racky Diaby pendant que celle-ci était au téléphone avec elle. Ces propos l'amènent à décrire le mis en cause comme un homme violent et colérique. ​ Une enquête attendue ​On ignore à ce stade si le suspect a été interpellé et quelle suite judiciaire sera donnée à cette affaire. Cette tragédie relance, sur les réseaux sociaux, le débat sur les violences conjugales et sur les signaux d'alerte qui précèdent parfois les drames. ​Les obsèques de Racky Diaby auront lieu vendredi 9 octobre 2026 à Faladjè. L’article Drame conjugal : Deux jours après ses noces, Racky Diaby tuée par balle en plein sommeil est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Only a madman will vote for Tinubu in 2027 — Amaechi
items.description: Rotimi Amaechi, vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has described President Bola Tinubu’s decision to remove the petrol subsidy as “reckless,” declaring that only a madman would vote for the president in the 2027 general election. Amaechi made the remarks on Thursday at the ADC town hall meeting in Edo State, where he urged Nigerians to reject Tinubu, accusing his administration’s economic policies of worsening hardship across the country. “I read on social media that it is in 2027 that we will know how many madmen we have in Nigeria. It is only a madman that can vote for Tinubu,” he said. “If you are not mad, then Tinubu should not win here.” The former Minister of Transportation also accused supporters of the president of being motivated by self-interest. Amaechi faulted the removal of the petrol subsidy, rejecting Tinubu’s description of the policy as an act of courage. He argued that the president’s decision to proceed with the policy despite having been advised against it amounted to recklessness. “There is a difference between courage and recklessness. Tinubu wasn’t courageous; he was reckless,” Amaechi said. The ADC chieftain lamented the rising cost of living, saying many Nigerians could no longer afford basic necessities. “People are not able to feed. Things are difficult,” he said, attributing the hardship faced by households to the administration’s economic policies. Amaechi also criticised Nigeria’s energy sector, arguing that the country had failed to harness its abundant natural resources to drive industrial production and economic growth. He noted that Nigeria had substantial crude oil and natural gas reserves, particularly in the South-South region, but had failed to translate its resource wealth into sustainable prosperity for its citizens. The former minister called for policies that would stimulate domestic production rather than increase the financial burden on consumers and businesses. He said Atiku Abubakar, the ADC presidential candidate, would introduce production subsidies to strengthen local industries, boost domestic production and ease economic pressure on Nigerians if elected president in 2027. The post Only a madman will vote for Tinubu in 2027 — Amaechi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pregnant woman and husband found dead in a room at Anloga-Kportorgboe
items.description: A 35-year-old man and his pregnant wife have been found dead in their room at Kportorgboe, a suburb of Anloga in the Volta Region. The incident has left residents in shock and struggling to comprehend. Mr Edwin Kwasi Vedzi, the Assembly Member of Anloga Kportorgbe Electoral Area, disclosed the information to the Ghana News Agency and identified the deceased as Daniel Agbenyegah, a mason, and his wife, Patience Awumee. Mr Vedzi said Ms Awumee, who previously sold eggs, would be between 29 and 30 years old and carrying a pregnancy of about seven months. “Preliminary information indicates that the man allegedly killed his wife with a knife before taking his own life, and we are waiting for the police to confirm this account, since the circumstances remain unverified. The throats of both the deceased have been slashed,” he said. He explained that further information gathered indicated that the couple had travelled on Sunday to visit the woman’s parents and returned on Monday at about 1100 hours, while the incident was said to have occurred roughly half an hour after their return. He also told the GNA that the couple lived in the house of the husband’s grandfather, along with other relatives. However, the neighbours said they were not on speaking terms with the occupants of the house and that nobody had noticed any altercation. Mr Vedzi said what led to the tragedy was unknown, as there was no quarrel between the couple that residents and neighbours were aware of. The Police later removed the bodies and deposited them at the Keta Municipal Hospital Morgue for further examination and autopsy. The Assemblyman urged residents to remain calm and to cooperate with the police in their investigations to establish the cause of the deaths. The deaths have left the Kportorgbe community in shock, with condolences going out to the bereaved families and loved ones as the police was expected to release details of their findings once investigations and the autopsy were completed.

items.title: Sport et développement : Dakar accueille un sommet mondial les 30 et 31 octobre
items.description: Prévu les 30 et 31 octobre 2026, le deuxième Sommet Sport et Développement réunira à Dakar des dirigeants, des responsables du mouvement sportif, des investisseurs et des acteurs du développement. L’objectif est de faire du rendez-vous olympique un levier d’investissement, d’emploi des jeunes et de croissance pour le Sénégal et l’Afrique, selon la Conseiller technique du président de la République en matière de sports, Diamil Faye. Dakar s’apprête à accueillir la deuxième édition du Sommet Sport et Développement, organisée dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026 du 31 octobre au 13 novembre 2026 entre Diamniadio, Saly et Dakar. Placée sous le haut patronage et en présence effective du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, cette rencontre ambitionne de prolonger la portée des Jeux au-delà de la compétition sportive, en mettant l’accent sur les retombées économiques et sociales du sport. Autour du thème « Sport et Développement : de l’élan olympique à un héritage durable », le sommet réunira des chefs d’État, des dirigeants du sport international, des investisseurs, des institutions financières, des entreprises et des acteurs du développement. Il s’inscrit dans la continuité d’une première édition organisée en marge des Jeux olympiques de Paris 2024. Le sport comme levier économique Les discussions porteront notamment sur la capacité du sport à stimuler les investissements, l’innovation, le tourisme, l’inclusion sociale et la coopération internationale. L’emploi des jeunes et le développement de l’économie du sport figureront également parmi les principaux enjeux de cette rencontre. Dans le document, le conseiller spécial du président de la République pour les Sports, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye souligne l’importance de préparer l’après-JOJ. Ce sommet doit ainsi permettre au Sénégal et à l’Afrique de démontrer leur capacité à accueillir de grands événements sportifs internationaux tout en construisant un héritage durable. Il estime que Dakar 2026 doit contribuer à créer de nouvelles perspectives pour la jeunesse, notamment à travers l’emploi et le développement des activités économiques liées au sport. Le sommet entend ainsi rapprocher les partenaires susceptibles de traduire cette ambition en projets concrets. Deux journées consacrées aux opportunités du sport La première journée, le 30 octobre, sera consacrée au Forum Jeunesse, Sport & Business. Des acteurs du sport et du monde des affaires y examineront les possibilités offertes par l’économie du sport aux jeunes Sénégalais. La diplomatie sportive, l’industrie sportive africaine, le financement, les infrastructures, le tourisme, le streaming, le sponsoring et l’impact économique du sport seront au menu des échanges. Le 31 octobre, un Dialogue de haut niveau réunira des chefs d’État et de hauts responsables autour de la contribution du sport au développement de l’Afrique et à son influence internationale. Des jeunes athlètes, entrepreneurs et créateurs pourront également présenter leurs idées et leurs ambitions aux décideurs. Les travaux devraient s’achever par l’adoption de la Déclaration de Dakar. Celle-ci doit établir un cadre commun destiné à prolonger la dynamique de Dakar 2026 et à favoriser des investissements sur le long terme. Préparer l’après-JOJ À travers ce sommet, les organisateurs veulent élargir la réflexion sur l’héritage des grands événements sportifs. Au-delà de leur organisation et de leur réussite, l’enjeu est de déterminer comment ils peuvent générer des opportunités durables pour les économies et les populations. Pour le Sénégal, les JOJ Dakar 2026 constituent ainsi une occasion de mettre en avant le potentiel du sport comme moteur de développement. Le sommet des 30 et 31 octobre doit contribuer à inscrire cette ambition dans la durée, bien après la clôture des Jeux. C.G.D

items.title: Trump rules out new Iran attack before US midterm elections
items.description: President Donald Trump on Thursday ruled out attacking Iran before the US midterm elections on November 3, saying Washington was holding “productive discussions” with Tehran. Trump’s post on his Truth Social platform followed a surge in oil prices on Thursday driven by media reports suggesting potential new US strikes prior to those elections. “I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect…we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections,” he wrote. “We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he added, without providing additional details. The Atlantic magazine reported on Wednesday that the White House had asked the Pentagon to develop options to strike Iranian targets that could be used before the midterms. The New York Times published a similar report on Thursday, saying the plans were being developed despite Trump’s “ambivalence”. The rise in crude oil prices has also been fueled by persistent tensions in the Strait of Hormuz — a strategic chokepoint for the global oil trade — as well as hostilities between Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia. In a recent sign of those tensions, an oil tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar reported being struck “by multiple projectiles,” causing an unspecified number of casualties, the UKMTO maritime agency said Wednesday. Polls suggest that US voters are strongly dissatisfied over rising fuel prices, linked to the conflict launched by the United States and Israel against Iran in February. The US leader has repeatedly insisted in recent weeks that the United States has effectively won the Iran war, despite ongoing unrest and a recent security threat that forced the withdrawal of American bombers from a base in England. But Trump’s claims that prices will fall as soon as the Iran war is over have so far fallen on deaf ears with voters. The midterm elections will shape the final two years of Trump’s presidential term as his Republican Party risks losing its current grip on Congress. Although Trump is not on the ballot, he is heavily involved in the campaign, holding numerous rallies in an attempt to limit the damage or even turn the political tide. Trump has warned he faces a possible third impeachment if Democrats retake the House of Representatives, and the White House is preparing for a slew of investigations into corruption and abuse of power. The US president also on Thursday sought to calm a furor over his comments at a rally earlier this week that Iran could “take out” the cities of Los Angeles and San Diego. Trump, 80, blamed the “fake and artificial news” for misinterpreting the remarks, which Democrats pounced on. “In actuality, what I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon and, if you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?” Trump said on Truth Social. items.title: Man, 87, jailed 20 years for defiling nine-year-old girl at Ofankor
items.description: An 87-year-old unemployed man has been sentenced to 20 years imprisonment by the Police Headquarters Gender-Based Violence Court for defilement. The nine-year-old girl he defiled at Ofankor experienced lower abdominal pain, painful urination and “faecal incontinence” because of the vagina and anal sex, police said. Yaw Gahornu, charged with two counts of defilement and unnatural carnal knowledge, pleaded guilty. He was convicted and sentenced on his plea. Gohornu is said to have had sex with the victim on many occasions through her anus and vagina. The court sentenced Gahornu to 10 years imprisonment on each of the two counts of defilement. Sentences are to run consecutively. The court, however, discharged him on the charge of unnatural carnal knowledge. It was noted that the accused person, a first-time offender, did not waste the court’s time and had also spent a month in lawful custody. However, it said considering the increasing nature of the offence, it would hand down sentence, which served as deterrent to likeminded persons. The prosecution, led by Chief Inspector Opoku Aniagyei, said the complainant was a 42-year-old trader. He said the complainant, the victim’s mother, resided in the same neighbourhood as Gohornu, in Ofankor, Accra. The prosecution said Gohornu’s wooden structure, where he slept, was located about 40 meters from the complainant’s residence. The court heard that Gohornu started luring the victim into having anal and vaginal sex with him from July to August 31, 2026, when he was caught in the act. On August 29, at about 1540 hours, the complainant returned from work and noticed some blood stains on the victim’s pants, the court heard. When the complainant questioned her daughter, the prosecution said she mentioned Gahornu having anal and vagina sex with her anytime she went out to play. Prosecution said after having sex with the victim, Gohornu would threaten to kill her if she told her mother. On August 31, at about 1600 hours, Gohornu was having sex with the victim when his granddaughter caught them in the act and reported to her uncle, who in turn informed the complainant. The matter was reported to the police, and a medical form was issued to enable the victim to receive medical attention. When she was assessed, the victim was found to be in stable condition but experienced lower abdominal pain, painful urination and faecal incontinence because of the vagina and anal sex.

items.title: Don de sang : Les filiales de Vista Bank Burkina mobilisent leurs agents pour sauver des vies
items.description: Vista Bank et l’association SOS SANG ont organisé, ce 8 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, une journée de don de sang au siège de la banque. L’initiative a mobilisé plusieurs agents de l’établissement, qui ont répondu à l’appel dans un contexte marqué par des besoins importants en produits sanguins. A cette occasion, Mohamed BA, Directeur Général de Vista Bank Burkina, a rappelé l’importance de cette mobilisation : « Donner son sang est un geste simple, mais dont la portée est immense : quelques minutes de notre temps peuvent contribuer à sauver une vie. À travers cette collecte, nous souhaitons encourager nos collaborateurs et, plus largement, chacun d’entre nous à faire du don de sang un véritable réflexe de solidarité. En tant qu’entreprise citoyenne, les filiales de Vista au Burkina sont fières de s’associer à SOS DON DE SANG et au CNTS pour contribuer à cet élan de solidarité au bénéfice des populations. » Cette collecte doit contribuer à renforcer les réserves disponibles au profit des patients. Jean Bosco ZOUNDI, président de l’association SOS SANG, a expliqué avoir sollicité Vista Bank afin d’accompagner le Centre national de transfusion sanguine (CNTS) dans la collecte de poches de sang, particulièrement en cette période où les besoins sont importants en raison du paludisme. « Nous avons sollicité les premiers responsables de la structure pour nous accompagner en termes de poches de sang en cette période de paludisme, pour pouvoir accompagner le Centre national de transfusion sanguine. Ils ont bien voulu nous ouvrir leurs portes ce matin » , a-t-il expliqué. Les agents se mobilisent en grand nombre-©Faso7 La mobilisation des agents des filiales de Vista Bank Burkina s’est traduite par plusieurs témoignages de donneurs, dont certains ont déjà une expérience régulière du don de sang. « Vu les nombreuses campagnes qui demandent de donner le sang et quoi qu'on dise, donner son sang, c'est sauver des vies. Donc si mon don peut sauver des vies ou redonner la santé à des personnes, c'est volontiers que je suis venue donner mon sang » , a témoigné Djamilatou OUEDRAOGO, agent à Vista Bank, qui effectuait son huitième don. Pour Prisca KONE, agent de Vista Bank, la démarche revêt également une dimension personnelle. Ayant déjà été confrontée au besoin de sang pour sa fille, elle dit avoir voulu à son tour contribuer à aider d’autres personnes confrontées à la même situation. « Moi particulièrement, j'ai eu besoin du sang pour ma fille. Donc c'est ça qui m'a motivée aujourd'hui à venir faire également la même chose pour d'autres enfants qui seront dans le besoin » , a-t-elle confié. D’autres participants ont également mis en avant le caractère volontaire et solidaire du don. Stagiaire à Vista Bank, Abdoul Akim CONGO a estimé que chaque occasion de donner du sang constitue une possibilité de contribuer à sauver des vies, notamment celles des blessés. « Si je peux donner mon sang, à chaque fois que je peux donner, je le ferai » , a-t-il affirmé, avant d’encourager les personnes aptes au don à franchir le pas. Même son de cloche chez Mazou SORE, agent à Vista Bank, qui donne régulièrement son sang depuis ses années de lycée. « C'est une action qui est totalement gratuite et qui en principe permet de sauver des vies. Donc c'est vraiment un plaisir pour moi de pouvoir faire ça ce matin » , a-t-il déclaré. Un nombre de poches de sang au delà des attentes-©Faso7 Du côté de l’équipe chargée de la collecte, l’affluence observée a suscité des attentes au-delà des prévisions initiales. Ousmane Gaméné, infirmier au Centre de transfusion sanguine de Ouagadougou et membre de l’équipe de collecte, a indiqué que l’objectif initial était de recueillir 50 poches. « On est venu avec une prévision de cinquante poches, mais tel qu'on voit l'engouement, on espère avoir plus que ça » , a-t-il indiqué. Cette mobilisation rappelle que le don de sang constitue un geste de solidarité accessible aux personnes en bonne santé. L’association appelle ainsi d’autres structures à s’engager dans des initiatives similaires afin de contribuer à réduire les besoins en sang dans les formations sanitaires. Faso7 L’article Don de sang : Les filiales de Vista Bank Burkina mobilisent leurs agents pour sauver des vies est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Burkina Naatilgué : ECIMOD-BF veut créer 1 000 emplois et formaliser 1 000 entreprises
items.description: ECIMOD-BF a lancé, ce jeudi 8 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, le projet « Burkina Naatilgué », une initiative qui ambitionne d’accompagner 1 000 jeunes vers la création d’activités économiques structurées. À terme, le projet vise 1 000 emplois et 1 000 entreprises formalisées à travers l’obtention du RCCM avec une phase pilote qui concernera d’abord 100 jeunes. Porté par Norbert Bangré, alias « Américain Gando », Directeur général de ECIMOD-BF et expert en cuir certifié, Burkina Naatilgué entend répondre à l’une des principales difficultés rencontrées par les jeunes entrepreneurs qui est le passage de l’activité informelle à une entreprise structurée. Selon le promoteur, de nombreux jeunes disposent déjà de compétences ou exercent un métier, mais restent confrontés au manque de formation, d’accompagnement, de débouchés et de structuration. Le projet veut donc les aider à transformer ces compétences en véritables activités économiques capables de générer des revenus et à terme, créer d’autres emplois. « Créer un emploi, c'est aussi permettre à une personne de créer une activité qui lui permette de vivre dignement et d’employer quelqu'un d'autre » , a expliqué Norbert Bangré avant de souligner que pour la première phase du projet il va s’appuyer sur 5 corps de métier liés notamment au savoir-faire artisanal et au secteur du cuir. Il s’agit de la cordonnerie professionnelle en fabrique, de la maroquinerie professionnelle en fabrique, de la tapisserie professionnelle en fabrique, du cirage professionnel des meubles VIP, avions et voitures de luxe, ainsi que de la cordonnerie-réparation des chaussures et du cirage. « Un entrepreneur ne doit pas forcément travailler seul », Norbert Bangré À travers cette démarche, ECIMOD-BF veut faire évoluer les bénéficiaires d’un apprentissage essentiellement informel vers une véritable professionnalisation. L’objectif est de leur permettre d’apprendre, de pratiquer, de produire, de commercialiser leurs produits et, progressivement, de formaliser leurs activités. « Nous voulons montrer que le Burkina Faso peut produire. Que le Burkina Faso peut transformer. Que le Burkina Faso peut innover. Que le Burkina Faso peut créer des entreprises compétitives » , a affirmé « Américain Gando ». Au-delà de la formation, le projet prévoit un accompagnement destiné à conduire les jeunes vers la formalisation de leurs activités. La création d’une coopérative dénommée « Coopérative Burkina Naatilgué » (COBNA) est également annoncée à la suite de la phase pilote. Pour ECIMOD-BF, l’enjeu ne se limite toutefois pas à la création individuelle d’entreprises. Le projet entend également favoriser la constitution de chaînes de valeur autour des différents métiers. Ainsi, un jeune pourra produire, un autre transformer, un autre commercialiser, tandis que d’autres pourront intervenir dans la communication ou la livraison. « Un entrepreneur ne doit pas forcément travailler seul », a souligné le promoteur, qui souhaite ainsi favoriser une dynamique collective entre les jeunes bénéficiaires. À long terme, Burkina Naatilgué ambitionne de dépasser le cadre des 1 000 premiers bénéficiaires. Le projet veut contribuer à faire émerger une nouvelle génération d’entrepreneurs burkinabè capables de créer de la richesse, de développer des entreprises compétitives et de transmettre leurs compétences. items.title: Burkina : Compte-rendu du conseil des ministres du Jeudi 08 octobre 2026
items.description: Le Conseil des ministres s’est tenu à Ouagadougou, le jeudi 08 octobre 2026, en séance ordinaire, de 09 H 00 min à 13 H 35 min, sous la présidence du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORE, Président du Faso, Président du Conseil des ministres. Il a délibéré sur les dossiers inscrits à son ordre du jour, entendu des communications orales, procédé à des nominations, et autorisé des missions à l’étranger. I. DELIBERATIONS I.1. AU TITRE DE LA PRESIDENCE DU FASO Le Conseil a adopté trois (03) rapports. Le premier rapport est relatif à trois (03) projets de décret portant respectivement nomination du Président, des Vice-présidents et de la secrétaire perpétuelle de l’Académie nationale des sciences, des arts et des lettres du Burkina Faso (ANSAL-BF). L’adoption de ce décret permet d’insuffler une nouvelle dynamique de fonctionnement à l’Académie nationale des sciences, des arts et des lettres du Burkina Faso en vue de remplir efficacement sa mission. Le deuxième rapport est relatif à un décret portant institution d’un championnat de football des régions dénommé « Ligue de la Souveraineté ». Le football burkinabè connaît une forte concentration de son élite dans les principaux centres urbains. Cependant, l’insuffisance et la vétusté des infrastructures sportives ainsi que le déficit de compétitions dans certaines régions constituent des freins à l’engouement populaire et à une structuration de la discipline. L’institution de la Ligue de la Souveraineté s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’Initiative présidentielle pour la relève et la promotion de l’élite sportive. Elle permettra de : déconcentrer progressivement les investissements sportifs ; renforcer la pratique du football dans les régions ; favoriser l’émergence de talents locaux ; contribuer à la cohésion nationale par la valorisation des identités et des potentialités de chaque territoire. L’adoption de ce décret permet l’institution de la Ligue de la Souveraineté. Le troisième rapport porte inscription de projets sur la liste des projets spécifiques du Bureau national des grands projets du Burkina (BN-GPB). Ces projets concernent la construction de : 20 centres médicaux communaux ; 20 maternités modernes ; 04 blocs opératoires au profit de l’hôpital militaire Halassane COULIBALY de Ouagadougou ; l’Institut du cœur. Prévues dans le cadre de l’Initiative présidentielle pour la santé (IPS), ces infrastructures visent à renforcer la souveraineté sanitaire du pays et à offrir des soins de qualité aux populations dans les meilleurs délais. Le montant global de ces projets s’élève à soixante-sept milliards quatre-vingt-deux millions trois cent trente-neuf mille cent soixante-six (67 082 339 166) F CFA. Le financement est assuré par le budget de l’Etat, exercice 2026. I.2. AU TITRE DE LA PRIMATURE Le Conseil a adopté un décret portant renouvellement du mandat du Secrétaire permanent de l’Autorité de régulation de la commande publique (SP/ARCOP). L’adoption de ce décret permet le renouvellement du mandat du camarade Modeste YAMEOGO, Mle 91 264 T, Inspecteur du trésor, au poste de Secrétaire permanent de l’Autorité de régulation de la commande publique (SP/ARCOP) pour une dernière période de quatre (04) ans. I.3. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE L’AGRICULTURE, DE L’EAU, DES RESSOURCES ANIMALES ET HALIEUTIQUES Le Conseil a adopté deux (02) décrets. Le premier décret porte approbation des statuts particuliers de la Société industrielle burkinabè de matériels hydrauliques (SOCIMAH). L’adoption de ce décret permet à la Société industrielle burkinabè de matériels hydrauliques de se doter de textes règlementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions, conformément à la loi n°025/99 AN du 16 novembre 1999 portant règlementation générale des sociétés à capitaux publics. Le second décret porte approbation des statuts de l’Institut de formation agropastorale du Burkina Faso (IFAP-BF). L’adoption de ce décret permet à l’Institut de formation agropastorale du Burkina Faso de se doter de textes règlementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions, conformément au décret n°2014-613/PRES/PM/MEF du 24 juillet 2014 portant statut général des établissements publics à caractère administratif. I.4. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE L’ECONOMIE ET DES FINANCES Le Conseil a adopté trois (03) rapports. Le premier rapport est relatif au financement additionnel du Projet d’urgence, de développement territorial et de résilience (PUDTR). La première phase du Projet d’urgence, de développement territorial et de résilience a permis d’obtenir une performance satisfaisante. En effet, toutes les cibles associées aux 22 indicateurs de performance ont été atteintes au 30 septembre 2026. Dans cette perspective, le financement additionnel du PUDTR vise à compléter les interventions du projet par un ensemble d’investissements structurants en milieu urbain et rural. Les principaux résultats attendus sont : la construction d’un bâtiment administratif (R+5) ; la construction et l’équipement de 2 lycées professionnels (R+ 3) ; la construction de 2 lycées (R+3) dans des communes urbaines ; la construction de 4 complexes scolaires en milieu urbain, villes secondaires ; la construction de 44 km de canaux d’assainissement ; l’installation de 600 systèmes d’éclairage public solaire ; la construction de 8 magasins de stockage de 5 000 m2 au profit de la SONAGESS ; l’aménagement de 150 ha de bas-fonds et 40 ha de périmètres maraichers ; l’aménagement de 6 Parcs urbains d’équipements sportifs et récréatifs (PUESR) ; la construction d’un Centre de formation et de transformation artisanale (CFTA). Les interventions du projet s’inscrivent dans les actions du Plan RELANCE et couvrent le territoire national. Le financement additionnel est d’environ 100 millions USD soit 55 milliards F CFA. Il est assuré par le budget de l’Etat et l’Association internationale de développement (IDA). Le deuxième rapport est relatif à un projet de Loi de finances pour l’exécution du budget de l’Etat, exercice 2027. Le budget de l’Etat, exercice 2027 a été élaboré sur la base des priorités et choix stratégiques budgétaires découlant des quatre (04) piliers du Plan RELANCE 2026-2030. L’élaboration de ce budget se déroule également dans un contexte national marqué par une bonne dynamique de reconquête de l’intégrité du territoire et les perspectives de bonnes campagnes agropastorales, ainsi que dans un environnement international empreint d’incertitudes. Dans la dynamique de mise en œuvre du Plan RELANCE, le projet de loi du budget de l’Etat, exercice 2027 se chiffre à 4 220,4 milliards F CFA en recettes et à 4 839, 4 milliards F CFA en dépenses, dégageant ainsi un solde budgétaire global de -619,0 milliards F CFA, correspondant à -2,9% du PIB nominal. Les recettes budgétaires totales de l’année 2027 enregistrent une hausse de 491,9 milliards F CFA par rapport aux prévisions révisées de 2026, soit un taux d’accroissement de 13,2%. Le Conseil a marqué son accord pour la transmission dudit projet de loi à l’Assemblée législative du Peuple. Le troisième rapport est relatif à un projet de décret portant création de l’Institut de formation agropastorale du Burkina Faso en abrégé « IFAP-BF ». La formation des cadres du ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’eau, des ressources animales et halieutiques est principalement assurée par deux établissements publics de l’Etat à savoir, l’Ecole nationale de formation agricole (ENAFA) de Matourkou et l’Ecole nationale de l’élevage et de la santé animale (ENESA). En vue d’une meilleure optimisation de la formation des cadres au service d’une agriculture nationale plus performante et en phase avec les réalités du monde rural, le Gouvernement décide de la fusion de l’ENAFA et de l’ENESA, avec la création de l’Institut de formation agropastorale du Burkina Faso (IFAP-BF). Cette fusion vise à répondre à des enjeux institutionnels, pédagogiques et opérationnels. Elle permettra également la mise en place d’une direction générale de coordination des actions de deux directions consacrées au volet formation agricole et au volet formation pastorale et halieutique. L’adoption de ce décret permet la création de l’Institut de formation agropastorale du Burkina Faso. I.5. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE LA COMMUNICATION, DE LA CULTURE, DES ARTS ET DU TOURISME Le Conseil a adopté deux (02) décrets. Le premier décret porte conditions et modalités de délivrance des autorisations d’exercice de la profession cinématographique et audiovisuelle. Ce décret est une application de la loi n°041-2024/ALT du 20 décembre 2024 portant organisation du cinéma, de l’audiovisuel et de l’image animée au Burkina Faso. Il vise à renforcer la professionnalisation des acteurs de la filière du cinéma, de l’audiovisuel et de l’image animée, à favoriser la création d’emplois formels dans les différentes branches de la filière ainsi qu’à promouvoir une régulation efficace garantissant un cadre éthique et équitable pour tous les acteurs. L’adoption de ce décret permet de renforcer la professionnalisation, la sécurisation juridique des investissements et la structuration durable de l’industrie cinématographique et audiovisuelle au Burkina Faso. Le second décret porte création de la Commission nationale du visa d’exploitation des films et fixation des conditions et modalités de délivrance du visa d’exploitation des films. Ce décret est une application de la loi n°41-2024/ALT du 20 décembre 2024 portant organisation du cinéma, de l’audiovisuel et de l’image animée au Burkina Faso. La Commission nationale du visa d’exploitation des films a pour mission d’émettre des avis motivés sur la délivrance des visas d’exploitation des films et sur la catégorie de classification attribuée. Ce décret vise à instituer un mécanisme de contrôle et de classification des œuvres filmiques en vue d’assurer la protection du public notamment les mineurs, la conformité des œuvres aux lois et règlements ainsi que la régulation et l’éthique du secteur cinématographique et audiovisuel. L’adoption de ce décret permet de garantir une régulation efficace, équitable et protectrice indispensable pour l’assainissement et la modernisation de la filière du cinéma, de l’audiovisuel et de l’image animée. I.6. AU TITRE DU MINISTERE DE L’INDUSTRIE, DU COMMERCE ET DE L’ARTISANAT Le Conseil a adopté trois (03) décrets. Le premier décret porte fixation de la liste des produits soumis à Autorisation spéciale d’importation (ASI) et à Autorisation spéciale d’exportation (ASE). Ce décret est une relecture du décret n°2025-1377/PF/PRIM/MICA/MEF du 2 octobre 2025 fixant la liste des produits soumis à Autorisation spéciale d’importation et à Autorisation spéciale d’exportation. Depuis 2022, vingt-trois unités industrielles de production de détergents et savons, deux unités de production de concentrés de tomates et une unité de production de craies ont été installées sur le territoire national pour des investissements estimés à près de vingt-six milliards (26 000 000 000) F CFA. Sept de ces unités ont bénéficié de l’accompagnement de l’Etat à travers des avantages du Code des investissements et de l’épargne publique mobilisée par actionnariat populaire. Ce décret vise la régulation de l’importation des produits similaires à ceux fabriqués par les unités nationales particulièrement celles évoluant dans le secteur de détergents, de concentrés de tomates et de production de craies en vue de soutenir l’écoulement de leurs productions sur le marché intérieur et de garantir la rentabilité des investissements nationaux consentis. L’adoption de ce décret permet de réguler l’importation de détergents, de savons, d’eau de javel, de craies et de concentrés de tomates au Burkina Faso. Le deuxième rapport est relatif à un projet de loi portant définition et détermination des entités économiques, commerciales et industrielles à caractère stratégique. Ce projet de loi est une relecture de la loi n°53/93/ADP du 20 décembre 1993 portant définition et détermination des sociétés et entreprises à caractère stratégique. Cette relecture vise à prendre en compte les nouvelles orientations de l’Etat et les exigences actuelles en matière de gouvernance des sociétés et entreprises à caractère stratégique. Les principales innovations de ce projet de loi sont : l’interdiction de la privatisation des entreprises publiques à caractère stratégique ; la prise en compte d’un nouveau critère de détermination des entreprises à caractère stratégique en l’occurrence le bénéfice d’un monopole ; le droit pour l’Etat d’entrer dans le capital de toute entreprise jugée à caractère stratégique. Le Conseil a marqué son accord pour la transmission dudit projet de loi à l’Assemblée législative du Peuple. Le troisième décret porte modification du décret portant approbation des statuts particuliers de la société d’Etat « FASO-YAAR ». Cette modification vise la création d’un poste de directeur général adjoint, chargé d’assister le Directeur général et la prise en compte du ministère en charge de l’Action sociale dans la composition du Conseil d’administration en lieu et place du ministère en charge de l’Environnement fusionné à celui en charge de l’Agriculture. L’adoption de ce décret permet à la société d’Etat « FASO YAAR » de disposer de nouveaux textes réglementaires en vue d’accomplir efficacement ses missions, conformément au décret n°2000-189/PRES/PM/MCIA du 17 mai 2000 portant statut général des sociétés d’Etat. II. COMMUNICATIONS ORALES II.1. Le ministre de l’Economie et des finances a fait au Conseil une communication relative à la mise à jour des tendances de l’économie du Burkina Faso en 2026 et des perspectives 2027-2029. Pour l’année 2026, le taux de croissance du Produit intérieur brut (PIB) réel est estimé en août à 6,0%, en hausse par rapport à la prévision de mars qui était de 5,7%. Cette amélioration est principalement liée à une révision à la hausse des performances de la production d’or ainsi que du niveau des recettes. Le dynamisme d’ensemble de la croissance en 2026 est impulsé par le secteur tertiaire contribuant de +2,7%, le secteur secondaire de +1,9% et le secteur primaire de +1,3%. L’inflation se situerait à 0,3% en 2026, en légère remontée de 0,8% par rapport à 2025. Le niveau général des prix devrait être contenu grâce aux mesures prises par le Gouvernement pour limiter la hausse des prix (contrôle des prix, interdiction d’exportation des céréales, etc.) et sécuriser les approvisionnements des zones à fort défis sécuritaires. Les recettes mobilisées à fin juin 2026 sont de 2 118,4 milliards F CFA contre 1 659,4 milliards F CFA à la même période en 2025, soit un accroissement de 27,7%. Cette hausse est attribuable à l’augmentation des recettes fiscales (+21,4%) et des autres recettes (+145,2%) ainsi que des dons. Quant aux dépenses, elles ont été exécutées à hauteur de 1 907,6 milliards F CFA à fin juin 2026 contre 1 857,7 milliards F CFA à fin juin 2025, soit une augmentation de 50,0 milliards F CFA. Sur la période 2027-2029, il est attendu de bonnes perspectives pour l’économie burkinabè. En effet, celles-ci se basent sur les hypothèses en lien avec une détente des tensions géostratégiques et une amélioration de la situation sociopolitique de la sous-région Ouest-africaine ainsi que d’une amélioration de la situation sécuritaire, la mise en œuvre du Plan RELANCE 2026-2030 et des conditions climatiques favorables. Ainsi, la croissance est projetée à 5,6%, 5,0% et 5,2% respectivement en 2027, 2028 et 2029. II.2. Le ministre de la Santé a fait au Conseil une communication relative à la commémoration du Mois d’« OCTOBRE ROSE » 2026, dédié à la lutte contre le cancer du sein. Cette commémoration se tient sous le thème : « Chaque dépistage est une vie sauvée et chaque vie de femme épargnée est une famille sauvegardée ». Elle constitue une opportunité de renforcer les actions de prévention, de dépistage, de communication pour le changement de comportement et de plaidoyer en faveur de l’amélioration de l’accès aux services de lutte contre le cancer au profit d’au moins 2 millions de femmes. items.title: El-Rufai fails to get order stopping ICPC, EFCC from freezing accounts
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri Former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai, has failed to persuade the Federal High Court in Abuja to stop the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and other anti-graft agencies in the country from freezing his bank accounts. In a ruling by Justice Joyce Abdulmalik, the court dismissed a suit filed by the former governor, who has been in detention, seeking an order restraining federal government agencies from moving against his assets. The court held that the suit not only lacked merit but was speculative, as no reasonable cause of action was disclosed against the agencies the applicant listed as defendants. Therefore, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF) were struck out from the case. In the suit he filed on February 24, El-Rufai prayed the court for an interim injunction directing the respondents to maintain the status quo ante regarding his assets. According to him, the order was necessary to prevent him from being placed in a state of helplessness. He insisted that the severance pay he received upon completing his tenure as governor of Kaduna State between 2015 and 2023 could not reasonably be suspected to be proceeds of any unlawful activity. He urged the court to declare that properties purchased from his severance pay were lawfully acquired. The banks the applicant prayed the court to protect from the respondents included Zenith Bank Plc, Naira Account Number: 1007158671; Zenith Bank Plc, Domiciliary Account Number: 507 1511327; Guaranty Trust Bank (GTB) Plc, Account Number: 0023824978; Access Bank, Dollar Account Number: 1396386493; and Access Bank, Naira Account Number: 1396382103. El-Rufai also sought a declaration that any attempt by the respondents to apply for, obtain or execute any interim or final forfeiture or freezing order, without first establishing a reasonable suspicion supported by credible evidence as required by relevant law, would amount to a breach of his rights. He relied on Section 17(1) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Related Offences Act, 2006, and the Supreme Court decision in Melrose General Services Ltd v. EFCC (2024) SC/1519/2019, to pray the court to declare that, as a citizen of Nigeria, he is entitled to the presumption of innocence and the protection of his fundamental rights. He argued that any action by the respondents seeking to circumvent his constitutionally guaranteed rights through ex parte applications that conceal material facts would amount to a breach of Section 36(5) of the Constitution and a violation of the principles of fair hearing. The post El-Rufai fails to get order stopping ICPC, EFCC from freezing accounts appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maresca says ‘feeling is fantastic’ among Man City squad
items.description: Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca says the “feeling is fantastic” among his players and they “don’t care too much about the noise” surrounding the club after it was found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against it by the Premier League. The club’s international players returned to training on Thursday, nine days after the Premier League published a damning report that stated the club had used “sham” contracts to disguise secret funding of more than £830m. BBC Sport reported this week that Maresca would address the players upon their return to domestic duty after news of the verdict broke while the majority of the squad were away with their respective nations. It is understood that the City head coach asked his players not to let the crisis that has engulfed the club affect their attitude and focus as the Premier League campaign gets back under way this weekend. “The feeling is fantastic, to be honest,” Maresca said in an in-house interview when asked about the mood among his squad prior to their trip to face Liverpool on Sunday (16:30 BST). “The players are excited for the next two games. But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league. The players are just focused on that. “They know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things. “They know their profession and they know that the noise is there, but they don’t care too much about the noise. They are just focused in this moment on how we can beat Liverpool and how, together with the fans, we can try to win in Anfield.” Maresca added he felt “calm” and his squad trusts the club “completely”. City have launched an appeal and have publicly maintained their innocence. The private communication to those with links to the playing staff at City has been equally as emphatic, it is understood. Speaking to Sky Sports, striker Erling Haaland echoed his manager’s sentiments, saying: “I care a lot about this place. I spent my first four years here, it’s a special place for us. I care a lot about City and the fans. I am a fan myself. I feel with them. “The fans will have a good time on Sunday – we have to stick together. We have to stay with each other and stay positive. No matter what happens in life, we always have to smile. Stay positive, look ahead, and try to win football games and enjoy the situation. “We have to stick together and spread the love to each other. Enjoy the ride and smile.” Erling Haaland is the leading scorer in the new Premier League season with five goals What have other Premier League managers said? As Premier League football returns following a three-week hiatus, managers of rival clubs can expect to be asked to comment on the City verdict during their compulsory pre-match press conferences. Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner will face the media on Friday but told reporters earlier in the week he hopes the process is completed “as soon as possible”. Glasner joined Forest from Crystal Palace in the summer and cited his experience of the latter’s demotion from the Europa League to the Conference League in 2025 after the club breached multi-club ownership rules. “Let’s wait until the final verdict is spoken, but my wish is just that this is quick,” Glasner said. “Because we didn’t know with Palace if we were in the Europa League or Conference League and then it was ‘you will hear on Thursday’ and then that became Monday, because it was always delayed. Then we got the final verdict 10 days before the Conference League started. “That’s why I think this must be [completed] as soon as possible. “There is still damage for the Premier League, not just in England. It’s a big topic all over the world, especially in Europe. “The most important thing is the integrity of the league because as soon as the fans can’t trust it, they won’t watch it any more.” Some manager news conferences were held on Thursday and Leeds head coach Daniel Farke and Newcastle ‘s Matthias Jaissle both steered clear of commenting at length on the matter. It is understood a number of clubs have already taken a clear stance for their managers not to comment. Coventry boss Frank Lampard – who played for City in the 2014-15 season – said the players will not feel they have lost their titles even if the club is stripped of them because it is part of their personal history. City have yet to be punished but BBC Sport has been told there has been little appetite from within the Premier League – both the organisation and its clubs – for past titles to be taken from them. “I have titles, and I don’t have my titles hanging on my wall at home; I have them in my head,” said Lampard, who won the Premier League three times with Chelsea . “You are competing against the best in the Premier League, and a lot of things are out of [your] control, but you are competing against the best, and they’re very hard to beat. “So I think it would be very hard to take someone’s title away as a player individually, as they should be in your head as opposed to in a beautiful glass cabinet or whatever. I know there are some who do that.” Lampard made 38 appearances and scored eight goals when he joined City in 2014 after 13 years at Chelsea .

items.title: Sam George warns FBI Director against taking sole credit for Ghana cybercrime operation
items.description: Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has cautioned FBI Director Kash Patel against downplaying Ghana’s role in a recent cybercrime operation. He warned that such an approach could undermine future international cooperation. His response follows a Thursday post by Mr Patel announcing arrests and seizures under the FBI’s global Operation Blackout, which targets scam centres accused of defrauding victims, including American citizens. The Minister objected to the post’s framing, saying it failed to acknowledge the leading role of e Ghanaian law enforcement and intelligence agencies, as well as the support from the United Kingdom’s National Crime Agency (NCA) and the FBI. “@FBIDirectorKash, as Ghana’s Minister responsible for Cybersecurity, I believe the fight against cybercrime is transnational and requires collaboration. Ghanaian law enforcement and intelligence led the Cyberhunt operations, with primary support from the UK @NCA_UK and the @FBI you lead,” he said. “To suggest the @FBI acted solely to execute this operation in your tweet undermines the potential for future collaboration. I expect that you will reflect on the benefits of our continued cooperation and act accordingly,” he added. Mr George explained that Ghana’s Cyber Security Authority (CSA), under his Ministry, worked with the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service and operatives from the National Security Secretariat to carry out a series of sting operations between September 25 and 28, 2026. He said the operations dealt a decisive blow to cybercriminals and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to tackling cybercrime. “The John Dramani Mahama administration is committed to stamping out cybercrime. We are grateful to our international partners, including the UK’s NCA and the FBI,” he stated. The Minister assured that the CSA would continue working with local and international law enforcement agencies to sustain operations. In his post, Mr Patel said the latest operation in Ghana had so far identified nearly US$10 million in losses and 89 victims, saying that more than 130 individuals had been arrested or detained, while over 300 devices were seized. He added that some of those detained were victims who would be repatriated to their home countries, and that investigations were ongoing. Mr Patel also reported that the wider Operation Blackout had resulted in roughly US$17 billion in seizures, hundreds of arrests of alleged scammers and the freeing of thousands of trafficked workers. He said more than 10,000 Americans had been warned before losing money, with an estimated US$670 million in losses prevented.
